title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Office Release Charge on a Block Bought Past the Ceiling
content:
| The block price against the credit ceiling standing on the program | The most recent invoice to fall due | The office release charge |
|---|---|---|
| carries the open position past that ceiling | stands past its due day | 3.0 percent on the excess |
| carries the open position past that ceiling | does not stand past its due day | 1.5 percent on the excess |
| leaves the open position at or below that ceiling | either | no office release charge is added |

The excess the rate runs on is the block price less the headroom the ceiling leaves, never below nil,
and the days past due are counted from the due day carried on the most recent invoice to fall due on the
rate program under the Demand Service Rate Programs.

**Both sides of the condition (hypothetical).** A block priced at 9000 US dollars on a program whose
headroom is 6000 US dollars carries the open position past the ceiling, the excess standing at 3000 US
dollars: where the most recent invoice to fall due stands past its due day the office release charge is
3.0 percent of 3000 US dollars, which is 90 US dollars; where it does not, the charge is 1.5 percent of
3000 US dollars, which is 45 US dollars. A block priced at 5000 US dollars against that same headroom
leaves no excess and attracts no office release charge at all.
